finding.title: Merge duplicate LearningProgramRepository test suites (learning_program_repository_test.dart + learning_program_service_test.dart)
finding.rule: Fowler duplication lens + TQ-1 (pyramid/test-suite hygiene, avoid redundant suites)

evidence.quote: test('programs have sequential ids starting at 1', () {
test('program ids are sequential starting from 1', () {

finding.why: Both files exist purely to test LearningProgramRepository (a ~60-line class) via LearningProgramRepository.instance, and both independently cover getAllPrograms, getActivePrograms, getProgramById (valid/0/out-of-range), getProgramByName (found/missing) and getProgramsByCurriculumType/getActiveProgramsByCurriculumType with near-identical assertions restated in different words. 329 combined lines maintain one class's coverage in two places that can silently drift — one file hardcodes 'daf_yomi'/'bavli' fixture literals the other lacks — and a reviewer who finds only one of the two would reasonably (and wrongly) believe it is the sole coverage. This is the concrete cost the AG-5 mispathing finding predicted: because neither test sits at the discoverable mirrored path, whoever wrote the second file evidently didn't find the first.
finding.recommendation: Merge into a single file at the mirrored path test/features/scheduler/domain/services/learning_program_service_test.dart, keeping the union of unique cases (the daf_yomi/bavli literal checks, testConfig/displayName field checks) and dropping exact duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one test file covers LearningProgramRepository, at the mirrored path
flutter test green; no unique assertion from either original file is lost

finding.title: Replace tautological isNotNull assertion on non-nullable testConfig field in learning_program_service_test.dart
finding.rule: TQ-8 (tautological assertion — asserts what the type system already guarantees, not real behavior)
finding.why: LearningProgramData.testConfig is declared as a non-nullable String, so expect(p.testConfig, isNotNull) can never fail — it's checking a compile-time guarantee, not runtime behavior. The test's evident intent (verify the '{}' fallback applied in learning_program_service.dart:86 when a seed omits test_config) is never actually asserted, so a regression that defaults testConfig to '' or breaks the fallback would pass this test silently.
finding.recommendation: Replace with a behavioral assertion, e.g. expect(p.testConfig, isNotEmpty), or explicitly assert the '{}' default for seeds that omit test_config.
acceptance_criteria: Assertion changed to one that can fail (verified by temporarily breaking the source default and confirming red, then reverting to green)

finding.title: Localize TransactionalEmail subject/body strings before wiring a real email provider
finding.rule: AX-2 — no hardcoded user-facing strings; EN/HE ARB parity

evidence.quote: /// Subject line (in English; localisation deferred to the email template).
'$parentName invited you to tutor $childName on Learning Tracker';

finding.why: All five email subject/body getters are hardcoded English with no AppLocalizations/ARB involvement, in a bilingual EN/HE app whose 1421-key ARB parity check would not catch this since these are plain Dart string literals, not l10n keys. Impact is currently nil — the only bound implementation is LoggingTransactionalEmailService, so no real recipient has ever seen this text — but the moment a real provider (SendGrid/Firebase Extension) is wired per the file's own WAKE-UP banner, Hebrew-speaking tutors/parents will receive tutor-invite/accept/decline/revoke/resign notifications only in English.
finding.recommendation: Route subject/body through locale-aware templates (e.g. Flutter's generated lookupAppLocalizations(locale) keyed off the recipient's stored locale, not the sender's device) before cutting over to a real provider; gate the provider cutover on this in the same Linear item that tracks provisioning.
acceptance_criteria: A Linear DNI-#### ticket exists gating real-email-provider cutover on localized templates
Once implemented, HE-locale recipients receive Hebrew subject/body; EN/HE parity is checkable the same way ARB keys are

finding.title: Split core/constants/curriculum_defaults.dart (1270 lines) — curriculum-label rendering engine misplaced outside core/labels/
finding.rule: AG-3 (400-line cap) + Fowler misplaced-responsibility / Rule-5 label-placement spirit
finding.why: At 1270 lines (3.2x the 400-line hand-written cap, confirmed via the AG-3 checker command in coding-standards.md: `find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) this single file bundles four distinct responsibilities: (1) stage/points/daily-target defaults (~45 lines), (2) an 800+ entry two-dialect (Ashkenazi/Sephardi) transliteration dictionary, (3) per-book hierarchy overrides, and (4) a ~900-line CurriculumLabels rendering engine with 15+ static methods (level(), fullPath(), stripStructuralPrefix(), containerCountLabel(), etc). 62 files import this module — matching AG-3's own stated rationale that oversized files 'exceed per-file agent read budgets... become dumping grounds' — so every consumer needing only the page-size default map pays the cost of a 900-line rendering engine living alongside it. That rendering/transliteration logic is exactly the kind of curriculum-label code Rule 5 designates for core/labels/ (where curriculum_label_renderer.dart and curriculum_label.dart already implement the same displayNameHe/En rendering pattern) — a maintainer fixing a Hebrew-label bug who greps core/labels/ first will miss half the logic. The bloat has already produced test sprawl: 4 separate test files (1213 combined lines) with 5+ duplicate assertion groups re-testing the same methods under different names (see companion test-duplication finding), concrete evidence that the file is too large for any one owner to track existing coverage.
finding.recommendation: Split into: core/constants/curriculum_defaults.dart (CurriculumDefaults + DefaultStageDefinition only, stays well under 400 lines), and move LevelLabels/CurriculumLabels/LevelValueKind/TransliterationVariant plus the transliteration dictionary into core/labels/ (new file, or merged into curriculum_label.dart), consistent with Rule 5's designated home for curriculum-label rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Enable the AG-3 line-count check (`find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) in `make audit`, at minimum warn-only for this file
curriculum_defaults.dart and its extracted sibling(s) each ≤400 lines
All 4 existing curriculum_defaults*/curriculum_labels*_test.dart suites still pass after the split with import paths updated

finding.title: Adopt or delete 6 of 7 unused NaturalKey.forX factories — mergers duplicate the exact key-format logic inline

evidence.quote: /// [DriftMergeStore] splits on `|` to decode composite keys, so the

finding.why: The file's own doc comment claims these factories 'replac[e] ad-hoc `$a|$b` string concatenations that were scattered across the merger layer' — but a repo-wide grep of lib/ and test/ shows forTrackConfig, forStageDefinition, forSettings, forBookmark, forLearningOrder and fromSingle all have zero callers; only forCompletion is used (1 call site, in completion_event_merger.dart). The mergers still hand-roll the identical shapes instead: core/sync/merge/stage_definition_merger.dart:48 builds `'${decoded.curriculumId}|${decoded.trackId}|${decoded.stageOrder}'` by hand — the exact 3-column shape forStageDefinition exists for — and core/sync/merge/learning_order_merger.dart:35 does the same for the 2-column shape forLearningOrder exists for. Because DriftMergeStore decodes these keys by splitting on `|` (the documented invariant at line 13-14), the format is load-bearing for sync correctness but is maintained by convention across 8+ merger files instead of the one factory meant to own it — a future edit to one merger's key shape without updating the others would silently break natural-key matching (double-inserts or dropped LWW comparisons) with no compiler check to catch the drift.
finding.recommendation: Either route the unused-factory mergers (stage_definition, settings, track_config, bookmark, learning_order) through the matching NaturalKey.forX calls, or delete the unused factories and correct the misleading doc comment. Prefer adoption since it centralizes the `|`-separator invariant DriftMergeStore depends on.
acceptance_criteria: Every core/sync/merge/*_merger.dart natural-key construction calls a NaturalKey.forX factory, or the doc comment at natural_key.dart:9-11 is corrected to stop claiming repo-wide adoption

A regression test asserts NaturalKey.forStageDefinition/forLearningOrder produce the exact strings the mergers currently hand-build, so a future format change breaks loudly in one place instead of silently
